Key Takeaways:

Nepal issues three-day high alert over Cyclone Arnab

Five provinces expected to face the strongest impacts

Heavy snowfall snowstorms and avalanche risks forecast in Himalayan areas

Road air travel and daily activities could face disruptions

Nepal has issued a high-alert advisory for October 29-31 as Cyclone Arnab, expected to make landfall in India, could bring heavy rain, thunderstorms, strong winds and snowfall across large parts of the country.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) warned that the cyclone's impacts are likely to be felt from the night of October 29, with Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces expected to face the greatest effects on October 30 and 31.

Forecasters say moderate rainfall accompanied by thunder, lightning and strong winds is likely in many places, while heavy rainfall is possible in some areas. Karnali and Sudurpashchim provinces could also experience rain and thunderstorms, with isolated heavy downpours.

title: Nepal gives owners of 25 Malaysia-selected agencies 35 days to report - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepal gives owners of 25 Malaysia-selected agencies 35 days to report  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepal’s Department of Foreign Employment has given people who have yet to respond to arrest warrants in foreign employment-related cases 35 days to contact the authorities, warning that their bank accounts and travel could be restricted if they fail to appear. The notice comes as the department investigates Malaysia’s selection of 25 Nepali recruitment agencies to recruit workers for the country.

The department had obtained authorisation from the Foreign Employment Tribunal to issue arrest warrants against the owners of the 25 agencies so it could question them in connection with the selection process. One of the agency owners, Rabin Gurung, has been taken into custody.

In a notice issued on Monday, the department called on those who had failed to respond to previously issued arrest warrants in foreign employment-related cases to contact the department or Nepal Police within 35 days of the notice’s publication.

Those who fail to appear within the deadline could face further legal action under the Foreign Employment Act, 2007, and other applicable laws, the department said. The measures could include freezing bank accounts used for financial transactions and restricting travel.

In the third week of August, Malaysia selected recruitment agencies from 10 labour-sending countries, including Nepal, to supply workers to the country. It selected 25 Nepali agencies as “principal agencies” and another 250 as “support agencies”.

The Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment directed the department to investigate why Malaysia had selected only 25 principal agencies from Nepal and take action where necessary. The department initially issued arrest warrants against the owners of the principal agencies to obtain their statements.

The agencies had earlier submitted six-point explanations to the department. Officials sought details about why and how the firms had been registered with Malaysia’s Foreign Worker Centralised Management System (FWCMS), the criteria and evaluation methods used to select them, and the process through which they were approved.

The department also asked which authorities had recommended or approved their registration, whether their inclusion in the system restricted competition among Nepali recruitment agencies, and whether any unlawful financial activity had occurred. It further sought clarification on whether the process violated the Foreign Employment Act, 2007, the Foreign Employment Rules, 2008, or other applicable laws.

The department has already halted the issuance of pre-approval for labour permits to the selected agencies until the investigation and legal proceedings are completed.

The agency owners, however, say they are ready to cooperate with the investigation.

“The Labour Ministry has held discussions with us only once. Following that discussion, we also submitted a written request asking that we be removed from Malaysia’s Foreign Worker Centralised Management System through diplomatic channels,” one agency owner told Kantipur. “We have already submitted all the documents the department requested concerning our companies’ transactions. We are ready to cooperate with the investigation.”

On August 22, Malaysia’s Ministry of Human Resources issued a statement announcing a new procedure for recruiting foreign workers. Under the system, Malaysian employers would be allowed to recruit workers only through agencies registered with FWCMS.

The system lists 25 recruitment agencies from Nepal, 99 from the Philippines, 40 each from Sri Lanka and Vietnam, 25 from Bangladesh, 23 from Cambodia, 10 each from India, Myanmar and Pakistan, and one from Thailand.

Nepal has objected to Malaysia’s selection process. Talks between the two countries at prime ministerial and labour ministerial levels have yet to resolve the dispute.

During a telephone conversation with his Malaysian counterpart, Nepal’s Labour Minister Ramjee Yadav urged Malaysia to include all licensed Nepali recruitment agencies in FWCMS and reconsider its selection criteria.

title: Nepal expects demand for 5.18 million flower garlands during Tihar - OnlineKhabar English News
description: Nepal expects demand for 5.18 million flower garlands during Tihar  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
Kathmandu, October 27

An estimated 5.18 million flower garlands of various varieties will be consumed across Nepal during this year’s Tihar festival, generating business worth around Rs 480 million from garlands alone.

According to data released by the Floriculture Association Nepal (FAN), the total turnover of the floriculture business during Tihar is projected to reach Rs 645 million when 4.3 million loose flowers and potted plants used to decorate homes, courtyards and offices are included.

Marigold garlands are expected to account for the largest share, with 4.5 million garlands projected to be sold at an average wholesale price of Rs 90 each, generating Rs 405 million.

Similarly, six million rupees’ worth of globe amaranth garlands, totalling 600,000 units at an average price of Rs 45 each, are expected to generate Rs 27 million. Another 20,000 chrysanthemum garlands, priced at an average of Rs 1,200 each, are projected to generate Rs 24 million. Mixed-flower garlands are expected to generate another Rs 24 million from 60,000 units priced at Rs 400 each.

In addition, sales of 3.5 million loose marigold flowers at Rs 30 each are expected to generate Rs 105 million, while eight million potted chrysanthemums priced at Rs 75 each are projected to generate Rs 60 million.

Commercial flower farming expands nationwide

According to FAN, commercial marigold cultivation has expanded significantly in recent years. More than 225 hectares of land across all seven provinces are now under commercial marigold farming.

Commercial production is taking place in districts including Kathmandu, Bhaktapur, Lalitpur, Dhading, Chitwan, Kavrepalanchok, Sindhupalchok, Nuwakot, Gorkha, Makwanpur, Ramechhap, Jhapa, Ilam, Dhankuta, Sunsari, Morang, Dhanusha, Sarlahi, Saptari, Siraha, Rupandehi, Kaski, Syangja, Banke, Palpa, Tanahun, Dang and Kailali.

The association said the expansion of flower production and markets has increased the income of farmers and floriculture entrepreneurs while contributing to import substitution.

Nepal self-sufficient in globe amaranth

Although Nepal still needs to import some marigold garlands, the country has become fully self-sufficient in globe amaranth, according to FAN President Rajesh Bhakta Shrestha.

Of the six million globe amaranth garlands expected to be in demand this year, four million are projected to be consumed domestically, while around 200,000 will be exported abroad.

Commercial globe amaranth cultivation takes place in Ichangunarayan in Kathmandu, Gundu in Bhaktapur, Godawari-Badikhel in Lalitpur, and parts of Dhading, Palpa, Kailali and Ilam.

October floods damage marigold farms, imports expected

Marigold demand has increased to 4.5 million garlands this year, up from four million last year. However, continuous rainfall from October 9 to 11 damaged marigold farms, according to the association.

Despite the damage caused by floods and landslides, domestic production is expected to supply around four million garlands. The remaining 11.11 per cent of demand will have to be met through imports, FAN said.

The association has urged consumers and traders to prioritise locally produced flowers. It said it was coordinating with relevant authorities to ensure smooth transportation from production areas to markets and fair pricing.

FAN President Shrestha said using locally produced flowers would have a positive impact on the overall economy.

“Prioritising domestic flowers during Tihar directly supports Nepali farmers and floriculture entrepreneurs while promoting local production, employment and self-reliance,” Shrestha said, expressing hope for cooperation from consumers and other stakeholders.

title: Climber falls nearly 5,000 feet to his death on Nepal mountain after reaching summit - CBS News
description: Climber falls nearly 5,000 feet to his death on Nepal mountain after reaching summit  CBS News
publisher.title: CBS News
full_article:
A German climber fell about 1,500 meters (nearly 5,000 feet) to his death on Monday, a day after reaching the summit of Ama Dablam mountain, according to a trekking company operator.

Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, was reported missing from Camp 3, which lies at around 6,200 meters. He had been resting after reaching the 6,812-meter summit on Sunday, before his planned descent.

"After a successful summit, he spent a night at Camp 3 on Sunday, and on Monday morning, his guide found him missing," Gokul Thapa, head of the trekking company Real Himalaya, told AFP.

Thapa said Waschiczek's personal trekking guide, Sonam Lama, had left him in the tent for a few minutes to return borrowed equipment, telling him to stay inside. When he returned, Waschiczek was missing.

Waschiczek's body was spotted by another Sherpa at Camp 2 at around 8 am on Monday at an altitude of about 4,600 metres, Thapa said.

The body was retrieved by helicopter during the afternoon and taken to Lukla, a town known as a gateway for mountaineers and trekkers heading to the Everest region.

It was then flown to the capital, Kathmandu, where a postmortem will be performed at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.

"Once the postmortem is done, the body will be handed over to his family members through the embassy," Thapa told AFP.

He said this was Waschiczek's second visit to Nepal.

"He had come to Nepal in 2024 for a trek, and his passing saddened us," he added.

Two Japanese climbers died last week on another peak in west Nepal, the Reuters news agency reported.

Ama Dablam lies in Nepal's Khumbu region and is considered a technically challenging mountain with steep faces.

This picture taken on April 25, 2021 show Mount Ama Dablam, which peaks at 6,812 meters, in the Everest region, some 140 kilometres northeast of Kathmandu. PRAKASH MATHEMA/AFP via Getty Images

This is the first fatality on the mountain this year.

Last October, two climbers, one French, aged 65, and the other South Korean, aged 66, died during expeditions there.

This climbing season, more than 300 climbers are attempting to scale Ama Dablam.

Mountaineers have died on other peaks this year.

In July, famed British Nepali climber Nirmal Purja and nine other climbers were killed after being swept away by an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak.

In May, two Indian climbers died on Mount Everest during a record-breaking period of ascents via Nepal's southern route.

In May, American climber Shelley Johannesen died in an avalanche on Nepal's Mount Makalu. Johannesen, co-founder of U.S.-based outfitter Dash Adventures, had successfully reached the 27,838-foot summit before she was struck by an avalanche at around 23,600 feet while coming down.

title: Cyclone Arnab alert: Andhra Pradesh braces for severe landfall, Nepal faces flood and avalanche risks - Open Magazine
description: Cyclone Arnab alert: Andhra Pradesh braces for severe landfall, Nepal faces flood and avalanche risks  Open Magazine
publisher.title: Open Magazine
full_article:
A cyclone gathering strength over the Bay of Bengal is threatening more than India’s eastern coastline. As Cyclone Arnab approaches Andhra Pradesh, forecasters are warning of powerful winds, intense rainfall and rough seas. Hundreds of kilometres away, Nepal is preparing for a different set of dangers: swollen rivers, disrupted transport, heavy mountain snowfall and possible avalanches.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast that the very severe cyclonic storm will cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, by the forenoon of Wednesday, October 28. Nepal’s disaster management authorities, meanwhile, have urged people and local administrations to remain on high alert from October 29 to 31.

Cyclone Arnab landfall: When and where will the storm hit India?

In its latest coastal weather bulletin issued on October 27, the IMD said Cyclone Arnab was expected to move west-north westwards before turning north westwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. The forecast placed sustained wind speeds at 115-125 kmph at landfall, with gusts reaching 140 kmph.

The storm intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm early on October 27, according to IMD officials cited by ANI. Its projected landfall zone includes the stretch between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, near Yanam.

The forecast remains subject to change as the system moves closer to land. Residents in coastal districts should follow the latest IMD bulletins and instructions from local authorities rather than relying on older forecasts.

Heavy rain, port warnings and a fishing ban in Andhra Pradesh

The threat extends beyond wind speeds. Coastal Andhra Pradesh is expected to experience intense rainfall, while Odisha has also been warned of widespread showers, thunderstorms and lightning. The IMD has cautioned that heavy to very heavy rain, including extremely heavy rain in isolated locations, is possible in Odisha on October 28.

Authorities have issued warnings at several Andhra Pradesh ports. According to IMD Cyclone Warning Centre director P. L. N. Murthy, Kakinada was placed under Great Danger Signal 10, Visakhapatnam and Gangavaram under Signal 9, and Machilipatnam and Nizampatnam under Signal 8. Other ports received local cautionary warnings.

Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea until the morning of October 30, ANI reported. The warnings reflect the danger posed by rough seas and strengthening winds as the cyclone approaches the coast.

Why is Nepal preparing for Cyclone Arnab’s impact?

The cyclone’s effects are also expected to influence weather conditions in Nepal. In an advisory issued on October 27, Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) asked the public, local governments and relevant agencies to remain alert from October 29 to 31.

The authority’s warning draws on a special post-monsoon bulletin from Nepal’s Department of Meteorology. Five provinces, Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini, are expected to face the most significant impacts on October 30 and 31, including rain, thunderstorms, lightning and strong winds. Heavy rainfall in some locations could trigger localised flooding.

Karnali and Sudurpashchim may also experience rain and thunderstorms, with heavy rainfall possible in isolated places.

Flooding, snowfall and avalanches: What are the risks in Nepal?

The danger is not limited to rain. High-hill and Himalayan areas face the possibility of heavy snowfall, snowstorms and avalanches, potentially affecting remote settlements, trekking routes and transport links.

The NDRRMA has advised tourists to avoid travelling to high-altitude areas during the alert period. People already in vulnerable locations have been urged to remain in safe places, while residents near rivers should avoid flood-prone areas. Travellers have also been advised to avoid non-essential journeys because road and air services could be disrupted.

The Kathmandu Post reported earlier that meteorologists were warning of a wider spell of unsettled weather across Nepal, with the potential for rainfall and snowfall after the monsoon’s withdrawal.

As Cyclone Arnab approaches India’s coast, both countries face different but connected weather risks. The immediate priority is to monitor official forecasts, heed local safety instructions and avoid exposed coastal or high-altitude areas until conditions improve.
